## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Revatīpetavatthu* (Pv 39) is a narrative poem preserved in the *Petavatthu* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. In this text, two hell wardens confront the deceased Revatī, explaining the karmic retribution resulting from her evil deeds on earth and contrasting her plight with the heavenly rewards gained through the religious merit of her husband.

 This textual relationship is corroborated by DharmaNexus, which detects extensive verbatim text reuse between Pv 39 and Vv 52 (§0.3–24.1 matching Vv 52 §3.1–26.1 with complete identity), as well as significant verse sharing with the *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541, §19.3–21.2) and the *Tikanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3) [DharmaNexus]. The commentary on the *Petavatthu* (*Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*), the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* likewise share substantial segments with the sutta [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, Revatī or her story is cross-referenced in numerous canonical and paracanonical contexts, including several suttas of the *Vimānavatthu* (such as Vv 15, Vv 19, Vv 22–25, and Vv 37), the *Surucijātaka* (Ja 489), the *Mittātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.7), the *Catumahārājasutta* and *Dutiyacatumahārājasutta* (AN 3.37, AN 3.38), and the *Sānusutta* (SN 10.5). DharmaNexus also notes an automatic, low-scoring cross-language alignment with a Tibetan medical treatise, the *Śālihotrīyāśvāyurvedasaṃhitā* (D4345) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
